name: Have you agreed the security control frameworks you intend to use with your organisation’s security function?
conditionsText:
The selected frameworks should be appropriate to the assets, architecture, risks and technology of the service, while also meeting organisational security requirements.
The guidance says this activity should be led by technical and security architects in collaboration with security teams that understand security frameworks and how to interpret them
requirementTitle: Have you agreed the security control frameworks you intend to use with your organisation’s security function?
requirementDescription: Has your organisation's security team been involved in deciding and agreeing which security frameworks the service will use?
why:
Your organisation may already have:
- required security frameworks
- standard security controls
- an organisational security controls taxonomy
- approved security patterns
- established security policies
- regulatory or compliance requirements.
Engaging the security function avoids individual services adopting inconsistent or unsuitable approaches and gives the project access to people who understand how the frameworks should be applied.
tasks: Identify any existing organisational security framework or controls taxonomy.
Discuss which additional frameworks are relevant to the service.
Agree which frameworks will provide the basis for the service's controls.
